rs-bl-dry.front: What happens to blood colour as it dries?
rs-bl-dry.back: It darkens and dulls, then looks brown. Rain lightens it.

rs-bl-tail.front: Which way does a blood drop tail point?
rs-bl-tail.back: The way the animal was moving.

rs-bl-round.back: The animal was standing or moving slowly (Tip).

rs-bl-volume.front: Deer blood volume and lethal loss?
rs-bl-volume.back: About 7% of body weight (about 4 L for 60 kg). Losing about a third may cause shock or death.
rs-bl-volume.diagram:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 292" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Blood volume. A 60 kilogram deer has about 4 litres of blood, roughly 7 percent of body weight. It may need to lose about a third, about 1.4 litres, before shock or death. A cup of 250 millilitres looks like a lot on leaves but is far less.">
<rect x="0" y="0" width="400" height="292" rx="0" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="200" y="28" font-size="19" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">How much blood is a lot?</text>
<rect x="40" y="80" width="90" height="160" rx="8" fill="#fff" stroke="#23261f" stroke-width="1.5"/><rect x="42" y="120" width="86" height="118" rx="6" fill="#c62828"/><text x="85" y="262" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">whole deer</text><text x="85" y="280" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">about 4 L (60 kg)</text><rect x="160" y="80" width="90" height="160" rx="8" fill="#fff" stroke="#23261f" stroke-width="1.5"/><rect x="162" y="200" width="86" height="38" rx="6" fill="#c62828"/><text x="205" y="262" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">a third</text><text x="205" y="280" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">about 1.4 L</text><rect x="290" y="80" width="70" height="160" rx="8" fill="#fff" stroke="#23261f" stroke-width="1.5"/><rect x="292" y="226" width="66" height="12" rx="4" fill="#c62828"/><text x="325" y="262" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">a cup</text><text x="325" y="280" font-size="14" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">250 mL</text><text x="200" y="64" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#23261f" text-anchor="middle">A deer may lose about a third before it fails (60%)</text>

rs-bl-cup.front: How to calibrate your eye for blood amount?
rs-bl-cup.back: Pour a cup (250 mL) of coloured water on leaves and look at it.

rs-bl-stop.front: Most common reason a blood trail stops?
rs-bl-stop.back: Clotting. Also fat or hair plugs, no exit hole, or a gut or muscle hit.

No blood does not mean no hit.">

rs-bl-nohit.front: No blood in the first 10 m. A miss?
rs-bl-nohit.back: Not necessarily. Search hair, tissue and tracks; wait and look again.

rs-bl-137.front: Heart or lung rifle hit: how far does a deer usually go?
rs-bl-137.back: Usually dead within about 137 m (150 yd).

rs-bl-bear.front: Tracking a wounded animal in bear country?
rs-bl-bear.back: Bears come to wounded animals. One tracks, one watches. Talk.

rs-bl-law.front: Can you follow a blood trail with your rifle after legal hours?
rs-bl-law.back: No. Following a trail with a firearm is hunting; no hunting after hours or with a light.
